entries.name: Neon Rainy Night · Cinematic Feeling
entries.description: A one-point perspective view of a narrow street on a rainy night, with vertical signboards hanging on both sides. The blue fog gets thicker as it gets further away, and there is a warm light at the end of the street; the reflection on the wet ground takes up half of the screen.

entries.name: Retro Japanese comics from the 80s–90s
entries.description: The celluloid painting shows people and cars speeding on an elevated highway at night. Looking up at the tall buildings, the taillights drag out two strips of light. The whole film looks like something from an old video tape.

entries.name: American comics · Trendy graffiti
entries.description: On a yellow background, magenta and cyan lightning split the screen, dots, spray paint, and exploding speed lines; a person punched out of the screen with a thick black outline, and a large onomatopoeic character next to it.

entries.name: Doomsday Industry·Dark Science Fiction
entries.description: There is almost only green; huge mechanical structures are layered into the fog, a large ring in the distance, a beam of light leaking from the top; a small man in red clothes and carrying a bag on the walkway faces away from the camera.

entries.name: Pixel Cyber ​​· Retro Games
entries.description: Looking down at a street full of signboards, an overpass crosses it, and at the end of the street is a large "City That Never Sleeps" screen, with people holding umbrellas, cars, and speeding cars, and it's raining pixels.

entries.name: Oriental Cyber ​​· National Fantasy
entries.description: A paper-colored sky, a bright red sun, and a row of cranes flying by; a five-story cornice pavilion by the water, hung with neon vertical signs of "Sleepless City" and "Restaurant" and a screen, and a cyan holographic halo on the top of the tower; behind are light-ink future towers and mountains, with strings of small red lanterns hanging on cables; a small boat on the water, and a man wearing a bamboo hat, their reflections melt like ink.

entries.name: Flat illustration · Rooftop at dusk
entries.description: The sky is changing at dusk, the city is silhouetted with three-story flat paint, a large neon word "Night City" is on the roof, a man and a cat are sitting on the edge of the building, and a light rail is passing behind.

entries.name: Wings
entries.description: A World War I air battle built with three.js, graded according to a 1927 positive color film copy: the sky is white, the black level is very deep, the entire body is amber stained, and the film gate shakes and scratches. "Wings" is most famous for its aerial battles where cameras are tied to airplanes, so most of the camera positions here are mounted on airplanes.
entries.fit: Silent film 3D air combat · Orthographic film black and white + amber dyeing

entries.name: The Broadway Melody
entries.description: Moving black gold and silver art deco song and dance poster: airbrush gradient, stepped proscenium, chrome-plated condenser microphone. Broadway in 1929 was the height of Art Deco, and this was another sound film, so sound waves were emitted from the microphone in circles.
entries.fit: Black gold and silver art deco song and dance poster

entries.name: All Quiet on the Western Front
entries.description: Kollwitz-style woodcut: large black, knife-cut white outlines, rough wood grain, Clawd overprinted with a single orange plate. Kollwitz's anti-war prints of 1921–22 emerged from the same war and the same grief as this film.

entries.name: Cimarron
entries.description: Panoramic view of an 1889 gold-toned albumen print: soft focus, slight lateral smearing, cream highlights and warm sepia shadows, grains of silver salt, hand-colored only by Clawd. The film opens with the Oklahoma rodeo of 1889, shot with the texture of a photo from that year, and this chapter remains monochromatic.

entries.name: Grand Hotel
entries.description: The circular lobby built with three.js follows MGM’s silver and black-and-white color scheme, with Clawd’s orange as the only color. The most famous thing about this film is the shot shot straight down from the top, with the corridor taken in circles. The entire set was built based on this shot.
entries.fit: MGM silver black and white 3D lobby

entries.name: Cavalcade
entries.description: Mucha-style Art Nouveau decorative painting: expanded brown outlines, flat pastel paint, mosaic background, and a halo behind the central figure. The movie opens with a family toasting to welcome the new century on New Year's Eve in 1899, so the halo is made into a clock face striking twelve o'clock.

entries.name: It Happened One Night
entries.description: Black and white rubber tube cartoon from 1934: ink lines of varying thickness, pie cut eyes, white gloves, cel flat overlay on grayscale watercolor background with film grain. Made in the same year as the movie, the road comedy's laughs fit the rhythms of a cartoon.
entries.fit: 30s black and white rubber hose cartoon

entries.name: Mutiny on the Bounty
entries.description: Copper engraving of an 18th century British Admiralty chart: rhumb line, compass rose, bathymetric figures, hand pastels, the Bounty is an illustration of a ship. The film is about a voyage, so the entire section remains on the sea chart.

entries.name: The Great Ziegfeld
entries.description: A rotating spiral "wedding cake" stage built with three.js, MGM silver black and white: satin, chiffon and ostrich feathers lined in deep black, only Clawd is the color. The 175-level spiral stage in "A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody" is the famous scene of this film.
entries.fit: Silver black and white 3D spiral wedding cake stage

entries.name: The Life of Emile Zola
entries.description: Newspaper movable type printing plus line-engraved illustrations from the 1890s: wooden movable type headlines, densely typed text, ink expansion and lack of ink on yellowed newsprint, and characters drawn with aligned lines. The most famous image from this film is the "I Accuse" front page of the Aurora newspaper on January 13, 1898.
entries.fit: Newspaper movable type printing + line engraving illustrations

entries.name: You Can't Take It with You
entries.description: 1930s WPA silkscreen poster: six-color opaque flat ink, color separation gradient, slight overprint misalignment, printed on cotton stock paper. The posters of the Federal Arts Project of 1936–39 are the film’s contemporaneous American graphic language and distance themselves from the newspapers of the 10th.

entries.name: Gone with the Wind
entries.description: Impasto oil painting: scraper color blocks, ridges of paint piles, the heat of Technicolor - from golden to blood-red sky, red earth, black silhouettes. The color of the entire film begins with "Gone with the Wind", and the first full-color picture is of Tara under the sunset.

entries.name: Rebecca
entries.description: Charcoal drawings on rough paper: velvety black, smeared gray, moonlight and fog erased with an eraser. Hitchcock's "Butterfly Dream" is a black and white gothic dream. The manor is first in fog and then in fire. Both can be drawn with charcoal.

entries.name: How Green Was My Valley
entries.description: Use opaque gouache in the golden and green color scheme of the original 1941 poster: solid color blocks, coal-black mountains of slag, Kyffin Williams-style thick dark mountains and intermittent strokes. The use of gouache rather than woodcut distinguishes it from Part 3; it shows the miners singing as they walk down the valley home.

entries.name: Mrs. Miniver
entries.description: Lithographic poster of the British Home Front in World War II: limited color palette of brick red, dark green, cream, grey-blue, with lithographic crayon grains for shading. At the end of the video: the whole village sang hymns in the village church whose roof was blown through, and the Spitfire flew over the hole.

entries.name: Casablanca
entries.description: What the film itself looks like: Arthur Edeson's studio black and white, painted as polished stills: soft-focus close-ups with eyelights, louvered shadows, shafts of light in smoke. Clawd as Rick is the only color.
entries.fit: Hollywood studio soft light black and white

entries.name: Going My Way
entries.description: Backlit Gothic stained glass: stained glass made of lead bars, human faces outlined in gray tones, Chartres blue and ruby ​​red borders, colored light shining on the church floor. Father O'Malley and the choir are embedded in the window, with a golden star above his head.

entries.name: The Lost Weekend
entries.description: The picture is typed: the characters of equal width fall on the pica grid, the gray scale depends on the density and overlapping of characters, and the ink color of the ribbon is uneven. Don went to the pawn shop with his typewriter, so the whole street was typed on the typewriter; Clawd typed it with orange ribbon.

entries.name: The Best Years of Our Lives
entries.description: Photojournalistic spread from 1946 Illustrated: thick black dots on coated paper, center crease, overprinted captions. The stripped-out B-17s line up to the horizon in deep focus; Clawd is printed alone on a spot-color orange plate, the only color.
entries.fit: Pictorial news photography half tone spread

entries.name: Gentleman's Agreement
entries.description: Graphite pencil in the style of magazine illustrations in the 1940s: first draw the composition lines, then arrange the lines in parallel over and over again, erase the dark parts, and erase the highlights. The scene builds gradually around a polite rejection at a hotel receptionist, with only Clawd in colored pencil.

entries.name: Hamlet
entries.description: Elsinore in real-time 3D, high contrast deep focus black and white: volumetric fog, wet stones, waves breaking into lace foam, silver salt particles. Take pictures of the castles, foggy battlements and rocks in Olivier's films; Clawd is the only color.
entries.fit: Black and white 3D castle in fog

entries.name: All the King's Men
entries.description: The wooden type relief printing of the Southern election poster: red, blue, and black inks are printed on beige paper. There are wood grains on the ground, the ink supply is uneven, the plates are misaligned, and the portrait has half-tone dots. This is Stark's campaign rally, printed by Clawd in Page 4 orange ink.

entries.name: All About Eve
entries.description: Al Hirschfield's Broadway comics: smooth ink lines with varying thicknesses, black block dialogue, and a lot of white space. Each person only captures one exaggerated feature. This film is about theater, and the party is drawn like a newspaper theater cartoon; Clawd is the only color.

entries.name: An American in Paris
entries.description: Raoul Dufy's watercolor: fast blue and black ink lines, underneath are transparent color blocks of cobalt blue, lemon yellow, and rose red. The lines and colors are never aligned. The ballet set at the end of the film was painted by Dufy, and both the Place de la Concorde and the dancers used his painting method.

entries.name: The Greatest Show on Earth
entries.description: Strobridge circus chromolithograph: chrome yellow, vermilion, cobalt blue flat coat, thick black outline, with halftone dots, misprints and lithographic grain. DeMille's marquee was painted as a three-circle poster, and Clawd played Sebastian for an alley-oop.

entries.name: From Here to Eternity
entries.description: High-key black and white in 1953: hard sunlight, dark sky, white foam, wet sand reflecting the sky, silver salt particles and halo. Take the kiss in the waves of Halona Bay; Clawd sitting on the lava and playing the bugle is the only color.
entries.fit: High profile beach black and white screen

entries.name: On the Waterfront
entries.description: Ben Shahn's social realism: trembling transfer ink lines, underneath are staggered flat egg-color blocks, workers with big hands and long faces, the colors are restrained to gray blue, brick red, and ocher yellow. Shane painted dockworkers and unions, which is the world of this film.

entries.name: Marty
entries.description: Television footage from 1955, played on a TV in a warm living room in the Bronx: scan lines, fluorescent halos, rounded convex screens, snowflakes, only Clawd had color. The original work was a live TV series, so it was shot on TV.

entries.name: Around the World in 80 Days
entries.description: Flat geometric cartoon from the 1950s: misaligned overprinting of color blocks and ink lines, discontinuous ink lines, crayon particles on cream paper. The 6-minute ending animation of this film is from Saul Bass, and it is this modernist painting method.

entries.name: The Bridge on the River Kwai
entries.description: General arrangement drawing pinned to drafting table: white lines, creases, water stains and red pencil revisions on Prussian blue background. The movie tells the story of a colonel who insisted on building a bridge, so he drew the bridge as his engineering drawing.

entries.name: Gigi
entries.description: Toulouse-Lautrec style chromolithographs: large flat areas, white outlines, splashes of ink instead of dots, and caricatured faces. Qiqi’s highlight moment was walking into Maxim’s restaurant and having all of Paris looking back at her. It was the Paris painted by Lautrec.

entries.name: Ben-Hur
entries.description: Procedurally generated 3D arena, widescreen epic lighting: desert sun, sand, marble and gold, Technicolor color grading plus 65mm grain. The chariot race is the most famous part of the film, so we just filmed the race, with the golden giant on the poster overhead.

entries.name: The Apartment
entries.description: Saul Bass-style white lines slide in on the black background, creating the most famous one-point perspective endless office hall in the movie, and then fill it with gray tones. The title sequence of this film was created by Bass; the only warm colors in the whole picture are Clawd and the key card.
entries.fit: Saul Bass line title · black and white

entries.name: West Side Story
entries.description: The 3D neighborhood of the Upper West Side under the red and orange Technicolor sunset is saturated and stage-like: red bricks, zigzag fire escapes, rooftop water towers, and poseable dancer puppets. Re-enact the movie's overhead shot of the opening scene, the Jets snapping their fingers, and the jump on the poster.

entries.name: Lawrence of Arabia
entries.description: Epic poster gouache with visible brushstroke direction, strong contrast between cold and warm: amber desert versus cobalt blue sky. The original poster for "Lawrence of Arabia" was painted by Howard Terpning using this technique.

entries.name: Tom Jones
entries.description: A satirical engraving of the Georgian era: Hogarth-style engravings of varying thickness and directional lines, painted with Rowlandson-style bright hand-painted pastels, slightly out of line, and added with a dialogue bubble. The movie itself is modeled after Hogarth's 18th-century England.

entries.name: My Fair Lady
entries.description: Quick, white ink lines, combined with pink and magenta watercolor smudges and dots, melt into white paper all around. The original 1964 poster is inked and pastel by Bob Peak; the scene is a black and white Ascot designed by Cecil Beaton.

entries.name: The Sound of Music
entries.description: 3D procedural Alps with a picture book feel: saturated emerald green, cobalt blue, snow white, sculptural ridges, cotton clouds, and grass waves blown by the wind. Reenact the opening helicopter aerial shot, and finally land on Maria spinning around on the top of the mountain.
entries.fit: Picture book-like 3D aerial photography of the Alps

entries.name: A Man for All Seasons
entries.description: Old Master oil portrait: smooth overdye sculpting, painted fur collars one by one, velvet highlights, gold chains carved one by one, with old varnish and cracks. Holbein himself painted Thomas More in 1527, and his composition is used here.

entries.name: In the Heat of the Night
entries.description: Three-color Risograph printing: dark blue, poster orange-red, fluorescent pink, with dots, grains and color misalignment; just printed with "less ink". Echoing the 1967 poster's orange-red heatwave base and black silhouette.

entries.name: Oliver!
entries.description: Victoria Toy Paper Theater: Hand-colored lithographed cardboard figures with scissors and white edges. Scenes are inserted in layers on sliding rods. Candlelight footlights under the gilded stage cast shadows on the scenes. "Oliver Twist" is a musical that was adapted to the small stage of a Victorian family.

entries.name: Midnight Cowboy
entries.description: Warhol's photo screen: The black dot photo layer is printed unevenly, misaligned and pressed on a loose flat color block. The background is silver, and the picture is repeated two or three times. There is a Warhol Factory-style party in the film, and the Elvis he painted is a cowboy.

entries.name: Patton
entries.description: A lithograph imitation of a 1940s U.S. Army war bond poster: graded flat-painted folds, dark outlines, dot shading, yellowed paper. Corresponding to the opening of "General Patton": the little general stood in front of a huge national flag that filled the stage and lectured.

entries.name: The French Connection
entries.description: The entire street under the Brooklyn Elevated Railway was built in 3D, and then adjusted to a coarse grain of 16mm: cool gray, dark parts with a bluish tint, high contrast, and camera shake. The most famous thing about this film is the car chase under the elevated railway. Only 3D could capture that kind of speed.
entries.fit: Car chase under elevated railway · 16mm grain 3D

entries.name: The Godfather
entries.description: In the oil painting of deep amber and ocher brown, only the area where the top light falls is warm: the dark part is a transparent thin cover dye, and the light-receiving edge is a thick coating. Recreate the overhead lighting in Gordon Willis's study in "I believe in America".
entries.fit: Rembrandt top light and dark oil painting

entries.name: The Sting
entries.description: Magazine illustrations from Leyendecker and Rockwell: block light, parallel brushstrokes, and sharp dark outlines. The chapter card in the film is modeled after the cover of The Saturday Evening Post, which was also used in the 1936 betting hall.

entries.name: The Godfather Part II
entries.description: A toned silver salt photograph from the turn of the century, hand-painted: sepia, soft focus, silver salt particles, mildew spots, cracked corners, and local touches of red, blue, and patina. Painting of young Vito arriving at Ellis Island in 1901, like Lewis Hine's photo.

entries.name: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
entries.description: Imitation of Edward Hopper's quiet realism: large flat light green walls, hard-edged parallelograms cast by low-angle morning light, and people separated from each other. Just like the ward in "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest": the order under the fluorescent lights is broken by an escape.

entries.name: Rocky
entries.description: Philadelphia in the early morning was made entirely in 3D, the 72 steps from the meat warehouse to the museum, adjusted to 1970s 35mm: cold blue sky, low golden sun, long shadows, mist, fine particles. Running up the steps and the surrounding mirror at the top are the memorable points of this film.

entries.name: Annie Hall
entries.description: "The New Yorker" single-frame cartoon: smart pen and ink lines, a few restrained pastel colors, a lot of white paper, and a line of handwritten captions below the drawing. Woody Allen's comedy is in the same tone as this magazine, and the lobster scene happened to be a one-frame joke comic.
entries.fit: "The New Yorker" single frame cartoon · ink line and light color

entries.name: The Deer Hunter
entries.description: Imitation of Andrew Wyeth's tempera paint: dry and fine cross-cut short brushes, low-saturated grass yellow, ocher brown, gray green, grass blades are painted one by one, and the sky is pale. Wyeth was a Pennsylvania painter, and "One Shot" deer hunting took place in the mountains above the steel towns of Pennsylvania.

entries.name: Kramer vs. Kramer
entries.description: A child's crayon drawing of a kitchen: crooked lines, color scribbled into and out of paper lines, labels and arrows, a sun with a smiley face. This is how Billy sees him and his dad making French toast.

entries.name: Ordinary People
entries.description: Layers of transparent watercolors: wet-painted sky and lake, water-stained edges, flowing flowers, blank paper as highlight, autumn gold and rust red paired with cold gray blue. Compare the quiet and melancholy Lake Forest autumn at the beginning of the film.

entries.name: Chariots of Fire
entries.description: A four-color lithograph imitating Jean Droit's 1924 Paris Olympics poster: classical human body, limited ink, clusters of lithographic particles, and uneven color registration. Chariots of Fire is about the 1924 Olympics, and the beach run comes to life like that poster.

entries.name: Gandhi
entries.description: Hand-made woodcut printing on cotton: indigo, madder red, turmeric and black engraving outlines, the color registration at the seams is misaligned, and the dye bleeds along the warp and weft. Hand-spun homespun cloth is a symbol of Gandhi, so the Salt March was printed on a piece of cloth.

entries.name: Terms of Endearment
entries.description: A family photo album spread out with faded Polaroid and Kodak snapshots: blueish black, cream highlights, white edges. One of the Polaroids comes to life and turns into a chase photo of a speedster on the beach. "Mother and Daughter Love" tells the story of mother and daughter for thirty years.

entries.name: Amadeus
entries.description: The profile figure cut out of black paper is trimmed with gold, sitting in a horseshoe-shaped golden box and red velvet, facing the stage with a starry sky. The highlight of "Mozart" is the opening night, when one scene contains the orchestra pit, stage, audience and Salieri in the dark.
entries.fit: Rococo Silhouette · Candlelight Golden Opera House

entries.name: Out of Africa
entries.description: Real-time 3D low-altitude flight: a chrome-yellow biplane flies over Soda Lake, tens of thousands of flamingos startle, amber haze light. What is most remembered for this film is Dennis taking Karen over Kenya, and her hand reaching out to the back seat.
entries.fit: 3D biplane flying over the East African Rift Valley

entries.name: Platoon
entries.description: Fast and powerful pen lines, pastel colors of olive green, earthy yellow, smoke ash and fire orange, leaving white space on all sides of the sketchbook paper. Like what was painted on site by an artist accompanying the army, it is close to the perspective of this film looking at the Vietnam War from the eyes of an infantryman.
entries.fit: Sketch of Vietnam War · Fountain pen and light color

entries.name: The Last Emperor
entries.description: The iron line drawing on the silk and the layers of azurite, stone green, cinnabar, and lacquer rendered, the palace of the boundary painting, and the thousands of officials kneeling in worship. The enthronement of the young emperor was a Qing palace ceremony, and the painting method used by Qing palace painters to record the ceremony was used.
entries.fit: Meticulous brushwork and heavy color · Palace painting on silk

entries.name: Rain Man
entries.description: Smooth airbrush gradients, hard-edged mattes, chrome highlights, and pink-green neon, layered with thin cyan count callouts. The 1980s style is paired with the world through Raymond's eyes: 82, 82, 82, a total of 246 toothpicks, and a card counting table.

entries.name: Driving Miss Daisy
entries.description: Solid and warm Rockwell realism: clean edges, visible brush strokes, afternoon sunlight filtering through oak trees, neighbors going about their business. The film is about two guys in a car in 1950s Atlanta, itself like a Saturday Evening Post cover.

entries.name: Dances with Wolves
entries.description: A soldier's field diary: pencil lines with varying weights, transparent watercolors, yellowed pulp paper, ink handwriting and pencil annotations on the margins. Dunbar keeps drawing in his diary throughout the film, so the grassland comes alive from his sketches.

entries.name: The Silence of the Lambs
entries.description: The fine copperplate lines and stipples are thinly hand-colored, and the plate numbers and Latin labels are printed on yellowed paper. The ghost-faced Hawkmoth on the poster should have been pinned to the specimen plate, and the same cold etching method extends to Lecter's cell.

entries.name: Unforgiven
entries.description: Impasto Western oil paintings in two tones: Remington's plains under the golden and red sunset, and his later years' blue-green night scenes lit by warm yellow window light. "Unforgiven" opens and ends with a silhouette of a person setting over a grave at sunset, and the final battle takes place in a small town on a rainy night.
entries.fit: Remington Western Oil Painting · Sunset and Rainy Night

entries.name: Schindler's List
entries.description: Cool gray, high-contrast black and white, coarse grain, and blown highlights; only the little girl's red coat and Clawd's orange have color. This is exactly Spielberg's approach: red coats and Sabbath candlelight are the only colors in the film.
entries.fit: Black and white film·The only red coat

entries.name: Forrest Gump
entries.description: Printed cards folded in parallel, white paper core, gray cardboard edges, shadows between layers and shallow depth of field, placed on a walnut desk. Forrest Gump sat on a bench and told his life into a story. When he turned a page, he had an experience.
entries.fit: Pop-up book · paper art on real desk

entries.name: Braveheart
entries.description: A page from a medieval manuscript: burnished gold leaf with stamped dots, lapis lazuli blue, vermilion, Gothic script, a window-like battle miniature in the center. "Braveheart" is a Scottish legend, and the "FREEDOM" at the end of the film is made into gold initials.

entries.name: The English Patient
entries.description: Watercolor sketches stuck in old books, sandwiched between maps, photos, notes and embossed flowers, the whole is the amber brown of posters. Emmaus's book of Herodotus, filled with drawings and notes, serves as the frame for the entire film, and the camera enters the swimmer's cave through a watercolor.

entries.name: Titanic
entries.description: The white lines on the Prussian cyanotype stand up, grow into perspective, and develop into a 3D ship in full color at sunset and into the night. The ship itself is the symbol of the film, so the same ship model was used in the shipyard drawings and the actual scene.

entries.name: Shakespeare in Love
entries.description: Learn from Nicholas Hilliard's Elizabethan court miniatures: opaque watercolor on parchment, ultramarine ground, shell gold inscription, white briar. The film takes place in Shakespeare's London, and the miniatures are that court's own portrait form.

entries.name: American Beauty
entries.description: Two images are cut together: first a clean, saturated, frontally symmetrical suburban house (red door, red roses), and then a low-definition DV video with a REC interface. Corresponding to Leicester's respectable suburbs and the plastic bag video captured by Ricky in the film.

entries.name: Gladiator
entries.description: The entire painting is paved with square stones and glass inserts: the stones along the outline are arranged along the shape, and the flat surface is arranged in rows, and the gold foil glass pieces will shine. The film itself is set in Rome, so the Colosseum and the Elysium Fields are made into Roman ground mosaics.

entries.name: A Beautiful Mind
entries.description: Two ostensibly handwritten mathematics: white grease pen on a Gothic library windowpane, chalk on a blackboard, numbers illuminated and connected by gold threads. This is how Nash sees patterns in the film: it's the light in his head, not the computer interface.
entries.fit: Window formulas with blackboard chalk + golden connecting lines

entries.name: Chicago
entries.description: The black stage is cut by hard-edged spotlights: in the six cells are the silhouettes of female prisoners with red edges, neon C, sequins and smoke behind them, and Clawd is in the white chasing light. This is the movie version of "Cell Block Tango", using the red and black colors of the poster.
entries.fit: Fox Stage: red and black spotlight silhouette

entries.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
entries.description: Soft watercolor and pencil landscape with deep plein air perspective and an ink line map on parchment. The concept art for the movie was drawn by Alan Lee and John Howe, so this journey is based on how the trilogy was originally drawn.
entries.fit: Alan Lee style watercolor + Tolkien map

entries.name: Million Dollar Baby
entries.description: Original 16-bit arcade fighting game graphics: health bar, turn timer, ROUND 1 / FIGHT!, combo count, hit pause and huge K.O. A movie about a championship boxing match becomes a round played out in arcade syntax.

entries.name: Crash
entries.description: A refined night scene photo drawn with code: overhead white and red car light tracks, sodium orange versus neon cyan, wet road reflections, out-of-focus spots, and snow that is only visible in the light. "Crash" ends with a rare snowfall in Los Angeles.
entries.fit: Los Angeles night view light rail + falling snow

entries.name: The Departed
entries.description: A flat, multi-layered spray-painted stencil with spray burrs and sagging, paint eaten into the cracks of the bricks, and a torn paste-up poster next to it. The last shot of "The Departed" is of a rat crawling over the railings under the golden dome of the State House. Street stencil graffiti has always loved drawing rats.
entries.fit: Boston red brick wall stencil graffiti

entries.name: No Country for Old Men
entries.description: Real-time 3D West Texas dusk wasteland: the sun presses on the horizon, long shadows toward the camera, low-saturated earthy yellows and gray-greens, fine grain. According to the light Deakins took for the Coen brothers, and the backlit person carrying the box on the poster.
entries.fit: 3D West Texas Wasteland at Dusk (Deakins Light)

entries.name: Slumdog Millionaire
entries.description: A TV studio with blue-purple and gold highlights, moving head light beams and lens flares; then it cuts to the saturated orange-cyan rooftops of Mumbai. The film itself cuts back and forth between the final question on a quiz show and the ghetto where Jamal comes from.

entries.name: The Hurt Locker
entries.description: One-page U.S. Army bomb disposal manual: uniform black lines, line shading, stippled sand, circled numbers and leads, exploded view of an IED, just a hint of olive green and sand. "The Hurt Locker" talks about procedures under high pressure, and the manual diagram is the drawn procedure.

entries.name: The King's Speech
entries.description: The interior has the texture of an oil painting with heavy wall texture: the cold gray-green multi-layered mottled wall in Rogge’s clinic, to the amber gold soft-covered broadcast room, spring-suspended microphones and thin golden sound waves. Follow the golden color of the walls and posters designed by Eve Stewart.

entries.name: The Artist
entries.description: Clean and shiny black and white: bright highlights, soft grayscale, art deco framed title cards, slight shimmer and grain; Clawd is the only color. The Artist is 2011's love letter to silent Hollywood, so it's even more polished than Part 1.
entries.fit: 2011 exquisite silent film black and white

entries.name: Argo
entries.description: A 1970s Kirby comic spread out on a production table: thick ink lines, Kirby energy bubbles, four-color dots on yellowed newsprint. The fake science fiction film in the film used the concept art drawn by Kirby, so the comic flipped from the fake epic all the way to the real runway escape.

entries.name: 12 Years a Slave
entries.description: An 1850s daguerreotype in a copper-framed velvet box, developed from the blank: a chair leaning against a violin, Clawd standing nearby with his head bowed. This is the photography of Solomon Northup's time, using only one object to tell the story, no people.

entries.name: Birdman
entries.description: Detailed 3D Broadway theater backstage, shot with a handheld long lens: warm tungsten lights versus cool fluorescent lights, and finally bursting into the glare of Times Square. "Birdman" is most famous for pretending to take one shot to the end, so the style of this section is that shot.

entries.name: Spotlight
entries.description: Pictures printed as newspaper dots are placed on the gray-green screen of a microfilm reader: scanning lines, rolling scanning strips, dust on the glass. The reporter in the film digs out the truth in this kind of archives, and the camera changes also cause the film to move horizontally.

entries.name: Moonlight
entries.description: A rich turquoise, magenta and moonlight blue oil painting portrait, the carved head is then repainted with brushstrokes following the body. Drawing directly from the title of the film, "Black boys look blue in the moonlight."

entries.name: The Shape of Water
entries.description: A real-time 3D rendering of a flooded bathroom and laboratory tank, immersed in green: flowing caustics, light beams falling from above, bubbles and a few warm lights. Del Toro's film was immersed in this kind of water, so the entire film was shot in the water.

entries.name: Green Book
entries.description: A "Southern Greetings" linen postcard comes to life: textured paper, saturated colors in airbrush, star glitter in chrome. The film, a 1962 road trip through the American South, takes exactly this kind of postcard path.

entries.name: Parasite
entries.description: An architectural cross-section of a hillside in Seoul: a glass mansion on the top of the mountain, a secret underground bunker, all the way to a flooded semi-basement, thin lines and soft material colors. "Parasite" is built on this class gap, and one picture can fit the entire film.

entries.name: Nomadland
entries.description: Pastel pastels on grey-purple paper, an open plain and an old RV, the sky changes from gold to rose to purple. "Nowhere" lives on the long and empty horizon at dusk, and the color powder makes it quiet and soft.

entries.name: CODA
entries.description: A polished sperm whale tooth on the oak table is carved with fine black lines, dotted with red, blue and yellow: Gloucester's fishing boat, a family pulling in the net, Ruby singing on the bow. It’s a folk craft native to the New England coast where the film is set.

entries.name: Everything Everywhere All at Once
entries.description: Four universes and four painting methods, all with real-time light stepping: the cold green IRS, the hot dog finger piano under the advertising light, the silent canyon with big-eyed rocks, and the everything bagel that turns into a black hole. Just like in the movie, jump between universes with big eye stickers.

entries.name: Oppenheimer
entries.description: Recreate the predawn Trinity Test Site in real-time 3D: a quantum illusion of approximately 720,000 particles of fireballs, orbits and waves, deep blue night against orange and gold fire, plus IMAX-style particles. "Oppenheimer" revolves around this light.

entries.name: Anora
entries.description: Pink, green, and orange neon tubes glowed, and their reflections dragged on the wet plank road and fell into the drifting snow, adding glow, out-of-focus spots, and particles. "Anola" goes from the Russian neon lights of Brighton Beach to a Vegas wedding sign, all lit up with tube lights.

entries.name: One Battle After Another
entries.description: The real-time 3D desert road goes up and down like a roller coaster, with three cars chasing each other over the slopes, shot with an ultra-telephoto lens, with heat waves, bleached glare and fine particles. What is reproduced is the most famous sequence of this film: the car chase on the ups and downs of the road.
